machine.shared: A development machine, with other work running at times; the A/B runs are alternated for that reason

build.tls: OpenSSL 3.6.3 (bundled, static); mbedTLS not built on this machine
build.note: CONFIG_DEBUG_TRACK_MEMORY is on (the .config of this machine): every allocation is tracked. A build without it does less work per allocation; that build was not measured here.

method.ab: Each benchmark of 7.25.5 linked twice: with the 7.25.5 libraries, and with the 7.25.4 module (compiled with the 7.25.5 headers) put before them. The two binaries run alternated, with a sync and a pause before each run; mean +- standard deviation (median). Figures of scope "change" are an A/B of one commit alone; scratch benchmarks are not in the tree. Source: performance/c/README.md and CHANGELOG.md "Performance, against 7.25.4".
method.tag_run: The benchmarks of performance/c/ and the ctest binaries test_topic_pkey_integer, test_topic_pkey_integer_iterator2 and test_topic_pkey_integer_iterator5, built from the 7.25.5 tree, run at tag time in rounds (n per figure: 5, or 3 for perf_c_treedb and perf_auth_bff), with a sync and a 3 s pause before each run and no CPU pinning. The per-second benchmarks drop their first and last second. Absolute figures of one machine: compare them with each other and with the reports of the same machine.

ab.label: Appends per second
ab.meaning: How many records one yuno can store per second in a key-indexed topic.
ab.method: Each module padded to the same .text size and linked 4 times with the libraries moved by 0, 320, 704 and 1472 bytes (removes the code-layout effect, up to 2.5% on one link); 20 rounds of each link, alternated.
ab.reason: Same speed, with the checks this release adds to every append: a flagged file, the tm order, a torn md2 tail, a stopped master.

ab.label: Appends per second, with a live reader
ab.meaning: The same appends while a real-time list follows the topic.
ab.method: Each module padded to the same .text size and linked 4 times with the libraries moved by 0, 320, 704 and 1472 bytes (removes the code-layout effect, up to 2.5% on one link); 20 rounds of each link, alternated.

ab.label: 400 000 appends into 20 000 files
ab.meaning: Filling a store: 2000 keys x 10 daily files x 20 rows.
ab.method: The timeranger2.c of each release, linked alternated before the same libraries; sync and a pause before each run.

ab.label: 600 000 appends into 30 files
ab.meaning: Filling one key of a topic that marks the tm order.
ab.method: The timeranger2.c of each release, linked alternated before the same libraries; sync and a pause before each run.

ab.label: Open a store as master (20 000 md2 files)
ab.meaning: The start-up time of a yuno that owns a large store.
ab.method: The timeranger2.c of each release, linked alternated before the same libraries; sync and a pause before each run.
ab.reason: The order markers are found in the listing of the key directory the open already reads, instead of one stat() per md2 file.

ab.label: Open a store as replica (20 000 md2 files)
ab.meaning: The start-up time of a yuno that reads a store another yuno writes.
ab.method: The timeranger2.c of each release, linked alternated before the same libraries; sync and a pause before each run.
ab.reason: Price kept, by decision: one more stat() per md2 file. A replica looks for the order markers on disk after reading each file, because a listing taken before could miss a marker the master writes during the open.

ab.label: Create 10 topics
ab.meaning: A one-time cost when a schema adds a topic.
ab.method: The timeranger2.c of each release, linked alternated before the same libraries; sync and a pause before each run. 20 rounds of each of 4 padded links.
ab.reason: Price kept, by decision: 2 fsyncs per topic. A power cut never leaves a topic whose files are not on disk. Opening an existing store makes no fsync.

ab.label: Change the topic_version of 10 topics
ab.meaning: A one-time cost when a schema changes the columns of a topic.
ab.method: The timeranger2.c of each release, linked alternated before the same libraries; sync and a pause before each run. 20 rounds of each of 4 padded links.
ab.reason: Price kept, by decision: 4 fsyncs per change. A power cut never leaves a new topic_version over a topic_cols.json that is not on disk.

ab.label: Query one minute by tm (migrated topic)
ab.meaning: A time-range read: 1 key, 30 files x 20 000 rows.
ab.method: The timeranger2.c of each release, linked alternated before the same libraries; sync and a pause before each run.
ab.reason: After `mark-tm-order` the query goes straight to the rows of the minute. The 7.25.4 figure is the query of 7.25.4 on the same data.
ab.short: tm query of a minute, migrated

ab.label: Query one minute by tm (topic not migrated)
ab.meaning: The same query on a topic created by 7.25.4 or earlier.
ab.method: The timeranger2.c of each release, linked alternated before the same libraries; sync and a pause before each run.
ab.reason: Price until migrated: a topic of 7.25.4 or earlier does not say that its tm order holds, so the query reads every md2 row of the key. `mark-tm-order` (19 ms here) migrates it once; see the CHANGELOG "Upgrade steps".
ab.short: tm query of a minute, not migrated

ab.label: Update a node in memory
ab.meaning: A change of a node that is not saved.
ab.method: The tr_treedb.c of each release, 4 link layouts, paired alternated runs pinned with taskset -c 6; CPU time of the process. 14 rounds x 4 layouts, N = 100 000.
ab.reason: An update deep-copied the node, with every child its hooks hold, for a check of the system schema on every treedb; now only on the system schema.

ab.label: Update a node and save it
ab.meaning: The common write: change a node and persist it.
ab.method: The tr_treedb.c of each release, 4 link layouts, paired alternated runs pinned with taskset -c 6; CPU time of the process. 14 rounds x 4 layouts, N = 100 000.

ab.label: Link or unlink two nodes
ab.meaning: One relation made or undone (the child is saved).
ab.method: The tr_treedb.c of each release, 4 link layouts, paired alternated runs pinned with taskset -c 6; CPU time of the process. 14 rounds x 4 layouts, N = 100 000.

ab.label: Create a node (half of them linked)
ab.meaning: A new node, saved.
ab.method: The tr_treedb.c of each release, 4 link layouts, paired alternated runs pinned with taskset -c 6; CPU time of the process. 14 rounds x 4 layouts, N = 100 000.

ab.label: Reopen the treedb
ab.meaning: Loading every node and its links at start-up (us_per_op as the benchmark counts it).
ab.method: The tr_treedb.c of each release, 4 link layouts, paired alternated runs pinned with taskset -c 6; CPU time of the process. 14 rounds x 4 layouts, N = 100 000.

ab.label: Forced delete of a node
ab.meaning: Removing a node, linked or not.
ab.method: The tr_treedb.c of each release, 4 link layouts, paired alternated runs pinned with taskset -c 6; CPU time of the process. 14 rounds x 4 layouts, N = 100 000.
ab.reason: Price: ~1 us per delete. The delete holds its events and keeps the column that lets a refused delete change nothing.

ab.label: Forced delete of a parent with 200 children
ab.meaning: Each child is unlinked and saved.
ab.method: The tr_treedb.c of each release, 4 link layouts, paired alternated runs pinned with taskset -c 6; CPU time of the process. 14 rounds x 4 layouts, N = 100 000.
ab.reason: The delete tells its children's events itself instead of holding two per child, and counts the children instead of building a reference string for each.

ab.label: Open 40 treedbs whose schema did not change (release against release)
ab.meaning: The start-up of a yuno with many treedbs: the everyday case.
ab.method: 7.25.4 with its own JSON load: medians of 4-8 rounds of an earlier run; 7.25.5: the tag-time run of the release as shipped (3 rounds). Not one alternated run.
ab.reason: A JSON file is read whole, then parsed: json_loadfd() made one read() per byte, 60 000 system calls for a 60 KB schema. And the literal is parsed once, not twice.

ab.label: Open 40 treedbs whose schema did not change (C_TREEDB alone)
ab.meaning: The same open, both sides on the 7.25.5 JSON load: what C_TREEDB itself changed.
ab.method: The c_treedb.c of 7.25.4 compiled with the 7.25.5 headers and linked before the 7.25.5 libraries, so both sides use the 7.25.5 JSON load; 10 alternated rounds.
ab.reason: The second parse_schema() of the literal is gone (~2.9 ms an open). A later fix of this release adds back ~0.9 ms an open (see ctreedb.same_literal_fix).

ab.label: First open of 40 treedbs (seed projection)
ab.meaning: A one-time cost: the first start of a new treedb.
ab.method: The c_treedb.c of 7.25.4 compiled with the 7.25.5 headers and linked before the 7.25.5 libraries, so both sides use the 7.25.5 JSON load; 10 alternated rounds.
ab.reason: Price kept, by decision (~24 ms an open): the record of the projection in progress, written whole with its fsyncs before the first write, so a crash in the middle is finished at the next open; the index of __system__ and the orphan search keep a draft from being taken for a leftover.

ab.label: Open 40 treedbs with a newer schema
ab.meaning: A one-time cost: the first start after a schema upgrade.
ab.method: The c_treedb.c of 7.25.4 compiled with the 7.25.5 headers and linked before the 7.25.5 libraries, so both sides use the 7.25.5 JSON load; 10 alternated rounds.
ab.reason: Price kept, by decision (~27 ms an open): the same crash-safe projection record, the drafts compared with the file in use, and the ownership checks of the projection.

ab.label: Open one treedb whose schema did not change: the last schema fixes
ab.meaning: The cost of two correctness fixes on the everyday open.
ab.method: A/B of that change alone, 8 alternated rounds, ms an open.
ab.reason: Price kept, by decision: one schema_diff() of the literal against the file, so a literal with other content under the same schema_version is said at every open.

ab.label: Write one agent audit record (300 bytes)
ab.meaning: What every command sent to the agent pays to be audited.
ab.method: The rotatory.c of each release, 8 rounds.
ab.reason: A record is checked once and written whole. 7.25.4 rebuilt the file name (localtime()) and ran access() + fstat() for each piece of a record.

ab.label: Write and flush one audit record
ab.meaning: What the agent does since 7.25.5: the record reaches the file before the command runs.
ab.method: The rotatory.c of each release, 8 rounds. A busier run.
ab.reason: 7.25.4 did not flush (a record could be lost in a crash); with the flush 7.25.5 is still ~5x cheaper than 7.25.4 without it.

ab.meaning: The ceiling of the event loop alone, no gobj layer.
ab.method: The yev_loop.c of each release, 8 rounds.

ab.label: TCP echo through the full gobj stack
ab.meaning: Round trips of a ~140-byte JSON message: C_IOGATE, C_TCP_S, C_PROT_TCP4H, C_CHANNEL.
ab.method: The yev_loop.c of each release, 8 rounds.

ab.label: TCP echo + one timeranger2 append per message
ab.meaning: The same, storing every message.
ab.method: The yev_loop.c of each release, 8 rounds.

ab.label: UDP round trip (64-byte datagrams)
ab.meaning: C_UDP_S read path.
ab.method: A scratch copy of the echo server of tests/c/c_udp_s_echo driven by a Python client, 20 000 round trips a round, 8 alternated rounds.
ab.reason: The read takes a new gbuffer only when the host keeps the received one.

ab.method: A benchmark written for the change (bench_publish.c, not in the tree): one event published to N subscribers of one gobj; only gobj.o differs (-O2); 8 alternated rounds at ~250 B, 16 at ~20 KB; mean.

ab.label: Publish one 250 B event to 1 subscriber with __global__
ab.meaning: gobj_publish_event(): the in-process message bus.
